sweep.notes: rows are mu_s (mu_k = 2/3 mu_s), columns tau_y in Pa; passage from the FE with the r 80 sleeve, breakout at the present 58 mm print depth with the arm lifting 4.9 N (sphere hold model)

belly.notes: Closed womb 148 L plus 68 L of docked tail air (2.1 L/kPa), pump air from outside through the snorkel. Print silicone lifts the belly 8 mm; growth air (about 8.4 L) lifts the belly to about 51 mm; the first contraction fills the belly to the 10 L cord stop (62 mm) and only then womb pressure rises, to 0.72 kPa at the slips. Each slip lets the baby take womb volume out, so womb pressure drops 0.1 to 0.25 kPa and the pump refills: the saw tooth is the contraction rhythm. When the baby is out the baby volume (about 11 L) has left the womb, the belly falls back to the folded rest (0 mm) and womb pressure to zero. Rise is 6.1 mm per liter (design v2).

window: Passes with sleeve friction mu_s up to about 0.6 (womb slips at 0.54, 0.63, 0.73 kPa for mu 0.2, 0.4, 0.6; at 0.8 the womb needs 0.94 kPa and stalls), a sleeve of r 80 to 90 mm, contractions of 0.7 to 1.0 kPa and baby pressure kept under 1.4 kPa; the gel yield stress does not touch the passage but sets breakout: with the print 58 mm under the gel surface buoyancy alone frees the baby only below about 21 Pa (42 Pa with a 4.9 N lift from the arm), and a bed 120 mm under the surface raises that to about 119 Pa.
